references.text: The Lord appears to Abram and promises the land to his descendants – the first land promise to Abram.
God renews the promise of land to Abram's descendants and emphasizes the extent of the land.
God confirms the promise of the entire land of Canaan as an eternal possession to Abraham's descendants.
The promise of the land is renewed to Isaac, Abram's son, with reference to the oath God swore to Abraham.
God renews the promise of land to Jacob, Abram's grandson, and continues the covenant promise through generations.
God sets the boundaries of the promised land from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines and from the wilderness to the Euphrates – a direct parallel to the land boundaries promised to Abram.
God shows Moses the promised land from Mount Nebo and reminds him of the oath He swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God describes to Joshua the borders of the land from the wilderness and Lebanon to the Euphrates – in agreement with the land promise to Abram.
Solomon's kingdom extends from the Euphrates to Egypt's border – a historical fulfillment of the land promise to Abraham.
The Levites praise God for choosing Abram and making the covenant to give the land to his descendants.
Stephen refers to God's promise to give Abraham and his descendants the land as a possession.
The author of Hebrews discusses God's oath and promise to Abraham, emphasizing that God confirmed His promise with an oath.
Confirmation that Exodus' journey is driven by the covenant concerning the land established in Genesis 15.
Narrative precursor: The call to the land (12:1) leads up to the covenant of the land (15:18).
The covenant in Genesis 15:18 is the theological foundation for the exodus described in Exodus 6:8.
The covenant regarding the land is transferred from Abraham to Jacob, confirming the promise in Genesis 15:18.
The entry into the land is the direct fulfillment of the oath in Genesis 15:18.
Isaac's stay in the land is based on the oath given to Abraham in Genesis 15:18.
Prophetic fulfillment: The same geographical boundaries from Genesis 15:18 are used to describe the gathering of Israel.
The promise of 'an eternal possession' to the descendants is confirmed to Joseph, based on Genesis 15:18.
Historical summary of the covenant in Genesis 15:18: Abraham received land and descendants.
A song of praise confirming God's faithfulness to the covenant in Genesis 15:18.
Visionary fulfillment: The division of the land as a fulfillment of the promise in Genesis 15:18.
New Testament confirmation that the oath given to Abraham (Genesis 15:18) has been fulfilled.
Historical confirmation of the covenant and the oath in Genesis 15:18.
Theological analysis: The inheritance comes through the promise in Genesis 15:18, not through the law.
Moses uses the promise in Genesis 15:18 as a basis for praying for God's grace.
God's faithfulness to the covenant in Genesis 15:18 is the foundation for future restoration.
